translations.text: May almighty God keep me, may the holy Lord help me! You created heaven and earth and all the wonders that are in them, my wonder-King, eternal Lord, great and manifold.
To you, glorious God, I commend my soul and my own body, and my words and my works, wise Lord, and all my limbs, guardian of light, and my many thoughts.

Show me, guardian of the stars, where it would be best for my soul to mark out the will of the Measurer, so that I may prosper with you in every matter; and raise up wise counsel within me, righteous King.
Do not let the arch-thief harm me in the shadows, though I have obeyed the Creator, the King of glory, the mighty Lord, more weakly than my own counsel would have had me do.
Forgive me in your grace, living God, my bitter evil deeds. I remember the remedy, glory of kings, and I will come to it if I may.
Grant me, my Lord, time and understanding and patience and remembrance of every one of the things that you, righteous King, wish to send me as a trial.
Now you know many wicked deeds in me; cleanse me nevertheless, Lord, for your mercy's sake, though I have committed more grim sins than God allowed me;
so I have need, nevertheless, to earn your favour, holy King of heaven, in the passing days, and to see and seek one life after the other,
May the gracious God then grant me eternal joy there and allow me life, though I made amends for my evil deeds later than the commandments of the holy heavenly power required.
Lo, you have given me much here. Set my hope on you, and my fearful forethoughts, so that it may stand firmly established. Raise up my mind, good King of spirits, to ready counsel.

Now I hasten to you, father of mankind, out of this world, now that I know I must, in a very short time. Receive me then, ruler of fates, into your glorious joy, and let me pass over, Lord of the beloved; help my spirit.
When there are too many hostile ones, granted to the envious [?], then I have comfort from the Lord, though earlier in my time I earned few favours.
Nevertheless, let angels take me into your presence, saving King, Measurer, through your mercy.

Though I have done many crimes day after day, nevertheless never let the devil lead me, your limb, on a hateful journey, lest they be able to rejoice in that plan, those overproud angels who thought themselves better than the eternal Christ.
They were false to themselves in the faith; therefore they must suffer punishment for a long time, accursed creatures.

Defend me and restrain them when the storm comes against my spirit. Help my soul then, mighty Lord; protect it and receive it, father of mankind, clearly resolved [?]; heal it, eternal God, Measurer strong in might.

My mind is now stained with sins, and at times [?] I am afraid for my soul, though you have given me many favours on this earth. Thanks be to you for all the rewards and mercies that you have given me.

I had earned none of this; yet in all this I wish to have courage, and to laugh and put my hope in it, to make myself ready for the soul's journey and hasten myself to the journey that I must set out on,

[?] to prepare my spirit, and to bear all that for God's sake with a glad mind, now that I am bound fast in my heart. Indeed, the Lord punishes me for some of those sins that I myself cannot clearly perceive.
I have angered God, the ruler of mankind; therefore I have been so bitterly punished before this world, since my misdeeds were great before men, so that I endure a deep martyrdom.

I am not a skilled judge, wise before the company; therefore I speak these words, eager in spirit, since misery befell me on earth from the beginning, so that every year I have always suffered (thanks be to God for everything!)
more troubles of mind than in other things, fear among the people; therefore I am driven out, wretched, from my homeland.
The solitary one, bereft of the joys of people, cannot live like this any longer, a friendless exile (the Lord is angry with him); he mourns in his youth,
and at every moment men help him along [?], add to his misery, and he endures all of it, the bitter words of men, and his heart is always sad, his mind sick in the morning.

I tell this tale of sorrow about myself most readily, and I have spoken of a journey, eager with longing, and I think about the sea. I do not know how [?] I could buy a boat on the sea, a ship on the waves;
I do not have much gold, nor indeed the friend who would help me on that journey, now that I myself cannot carry out my wish because of my poverty.
A tree may grow, await its fate and put out branches; but because of reproach I cannot love with my heart anyone of mankind, any man in my homeland. Alas, my Lord, mighty protector!
Though I am sick at heart, bitterly angered, the remedy lies with you after this life. In the light, I, a destitute man, cannot in any way live [?] on earth without hardships;
When I had friendship with strangers, [?] there was always sorrow for me, constantly, as the reward of love, as I have lived until now.
Still, the best thing, when a man cannot himself change his fate, is that he should then endure it well.
